claims.text: The proposed intervention combines a standard EAM reference with a machine-learned delta correction.
The delta correction is trained on ab initio molecular-dynamics data from the liquid state.
The hybrid potential captures many-body interactions that are absent from traditional EAM formulations.
Standard EAM fails to represent the diverse atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid.
Training on disordered liquid configurations will align the reference potential more closely with the ab initio configuration space.
The delta correction enhances reference–target phase-space overlap during thermodynamic integration.
The hybrid potential will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 40–50% relative to TOR-TILD's pure EAM references.
The target material is equimolar Cr–Fe–Mn–Ni in both solid and liquid states.
The relevant high-melting-temperature regime for equimolar Cr–Fe–Mn–Ni is approximately 3000 K.
The training dataset must substantially sample disordered liquid configurations.
The machine-learned delta term continuously modifies EAM-predicted energies using configurational and many-body information.
Pure EAM produces narrow configurational sampling, whereas the ab initio liquid has a broadly distributed configuration space.
The hybrid reference will produce solid–liquid free-energy estimates that converge more closely to direct ab initio benchmarks.
TOR-TILD's pure EAM reference has limited ability to represent the ab initio liquid's atomic configurations.
The approach may extend from equimolar Cr–Fe–Mn–Ni to similar multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Application at lower temperatures or different compositions may require recalibration.
A controlled benchmark will compare pure-EAM and hybrid-reference thermodynamic integration for the same equimolar Cr–Fe–Mn–Ni system.

Failure to obtain a statistically significant mismatch reduction of approximately 40–50% or greater, or failure to move the free-energy result closer to the ab initio benchmark, will falsify the hypothesis.
